mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ltc1, Ltc2a, Ltc3a, Ltc4a, Ltc5, Ltc6a, Ltc7
mechanism_claims.claim_text: All seven latarcins bind lipid membranes and fold into amphiphilic alpha-helices in DMPC/DMPG vesicles, with peptide-specific helicity values summarized in Table 2.
direct_assay_types: solution circular dichroism in DMPC/DMPG vesicles

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=4:2.2. Circular Dichroism Spectroscopy; xml:fig=2:Figure 2; xml:table=2

mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports membrane binding/folding, not a single intracellular molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: OCD and solid-state 15N-NMR classify the membrane-bound helices as surface-bound, tilted, slightly tilted, or aggregated depending on the peptide; Ltc2a is the most tilted and Ltc6a shows aggregation/perturbation.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=6:2.6. Oriented Circular Dichroism; xml:sec=7:2.7. Solid-State NMR; xml:fig=6:Figure 6; xml:fig=7:Figure 7; xml:table=2

mechanism_claims.limitations: Orientation/aggregation data describe membrane interaction state; they do not establish a receptor or enzyme target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ANTS/DPX leakage assays show peptide-dependent permeabilization of POPC/POPG model membranes, with Ltc2a high leakage and Ltc6a/Ltc7 high model-membrane leakage despite weak antimicrobial/hemolytic phenotypes.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=10:2.5. Vesicle Leakage Activity; xml:fig=5:Figure 5; xml:table=2

mechanism_claims.limitations: Leakage is model-membrane evidence and does not prove equivalent permeabilization in every bacterial species.

caution_findings.finding: The article suggests some active latarcins may act slowly or translocate toward intracellular targets, but no direct intracellular target assay is performed.
Supplementary Figure S3/prose report no pairwise leakage synergy; this limits combination-mechanism claims.
